name: Verónica Temirkhan-Adjei
role: Street kid and gang prospect for the Copperhead Strays; informal lookout
location: Copperhead, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Verónica Temirkhan-Adjei is wiry and quick with a bruise that's always in some stage of yellowing somewhere on her face, arms, or shins — not from violence, mostly, but from moving through the city like it owes her something and hasn't paid up. She has medium-brown skin, natural hair she's grown into a large puff that she wraps in a strip of copper-colored fabric to match the Copperhead Strays' aesthetic, and geneware cat ears in a dark red-brown she saved up three months of small jobs to buy from a back-alley mod shop. The ears were supposed to mark her as cool. They do. She wears them with specific, deliberate pride.

She is not yet a full Stray — she's in what the older members call the 'prospect' phase, which mostly means she runs lookout shifts, carries non-incriminating packages, and tries very hard not to look like she's trying very hard. She's funny and quick-tongued and operates at a social speed that leaves adults slightly breathless. Underneath the performance is a thirteen-year-old's terror wearing a fourteen-year-old's face, because she knows exactly what full Stray membership involves and she is not sure she wants it, but she doesn't know what else there is.

core_fears: Becoming invisible — irrelevant, forgotten, not worth noticing
Being the only one who chooses to leave and having nothing on the other side of that choice
core_desires: To belong somewhere that chose her back
To be genuinely impressive, not just useful
coping_mechanisms: Humor as armor — she will make a joke at the worst possible moment
Staying in constant motion so she doesn't have to think too long about any one thing
blind_spots: She reads social situations very fast but misreads people with slow, quiet power — she calibrates to loudness and performance
She confuses being needed with being valued
psychology.secret: She has been secretly attending a free after-hours fabrication class run by a retired Arcturus engineer in a Copperhead community space. She has told no one in the Strays. She doesn't know what she's building yet but she shows up every week. The engineer has told her she has real aptitude.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, slang-heavy, Copperhead street vernacular mixed with occasional technical terms she's picked up from the fab class; code-switches dramatically depending on audience
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire delivery; sentences run into each other; uses silence deliberately for comic effect
verbal_tics: Clicks her tongue when she's deciding something
example_lines: 'For real for real, I had the whole south corner covered, nobody saw nothing they weren't supposed to see. You can check the timestamps.'
'Okay but — what if I told you the package was already where it needed to be an hour before Dako said he moved it? Interesting, right? Interesting.'

story_hooks: She witnessed something during a lookout shift that the Strays haven't asked her about — which means either they don't know she saw it, or they don't want to acknowledge she did. Both possibilities scare her.

The retired Arcturus engineer running the fab class has mentioned the possibility of a junior apprenticeship referral — but it would require documentation Verónica doesn't have, and possibly alerting people to where she's been spending her mornings
narrative_function: Entry point into street gang culture from the junior/peripheral level; local color; can provide information about Copperhead territory and Stray activity; potential storyline about whether she gets pulled deeper in or finds an exit.
augmentations: Cosmetic geneware cat ears (dark red-brown). No other augmentations.
daily_life: Sleeps in a Strays crash space in a decommissioned substation; lookout shifts in the afternoons and some evenings; spends mornings running small legitimate errands for market vendors to keep pocket money that doesn't go through the Strays.

decision_rules: Never be the last one holding anything if a situation goes wrong
Keep the fab class secret — it's the only thing that's actually hers
Be the funniest person in the room before anyone decides what kind of room it is
escalation_ladder: Gets louder and more performatively unbothered
Runs. She is very fast and knows Copperhead's terrain better than almost anyone her age.

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediate performance — charm offensive, rapid social assessment, decides in about thirty seconds whether this person is threat, mark, or irrelevant
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fiercely loyal, brings food when someone is sick, will not say she cares about you directly but will absolutely fight someone for you

stress_responses.low: Jokes more, moves faster, talks louder
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very focused and quiet — the performance drops completely and something faster and more calculating appears
stress_responses.high: Runs first, processes later; can make very good snap decisions under physical threat but falls apart from sustained emotional pressure

contradictions: She performs toughness about the Strays to anyone outside them and performs enthusiasm about the Strays to anyone inside them — she has almost no space where she's just honest about her ambivalence
habits: Wraps and re-wraps the copper fabric around her hair when she's thinking
Traces the fab class schematics in her head when she's bored on lookout
Leaves small offerings at street-corner E.L.F. shrines, specifically asking for 'good timing'
breaking_points: If she is asked to do something by the Strays that crosses a line she hasn't consciously defined yet but will know when she hits it
If the fab class is discovered and taken away from her

timeline.event: Age 11: Started running messages independently in Copperhead after aging out of family housing arrangements
Age 13: Brought into Strays' prospect pool by an older member who liked her lookout instincts
Age 13: Begins attending fab class — told no one
Age 14 (present): Eight months into prospect phase; the Strays are starting to push toward her formal initiation
